cards.back: Yes — o instanceof int[] is a legal type comparison
cards.extra: Arrays are reference types, and JLS 15.20.2 allows any ReferenceType on the right, including an array type. It checks the array's actual component type, so new int[3] passes int[] but not Object[] — arrays are covariant, so new String[1] instanceof Object[] is true.
cards.example:
Object a = new int[3];
boolean hit = a instanceof int[];      // true
boolean miss = a instanceof Object[];  // false

cards.front: Why is 1 instanceof Integer a compile error?
cards.back: The left operand must be a reference type (or the null type) — no boxing happens here
cards.extra: JLS 15.20.2 requires the left operand's type to be a reference type or the null type, or a compile-time error occurs. javac reports unexpected type: required reference, found int. Box it yourself: Integer.valueOf(1) instanceof Integer compiles.
cards.example:
int i = 1;
boolean b = i instanceof Integer;             // error: required reference, found int
boolean ok = Integer.valueOf(i) instanceof Integer;  // true
